operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order exempts Thomas A. Jaggar, Jr., from compulsory retirement for age and fixes its own end in the sentence "hereby further exempt the said Thomas A. Jaggar, Jr., from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending July 31, 1940". The exemption therefore ran through July 31, 1940, and that date is recorded as the first end, inclusive; the exclusive reading (the exemption ends as July 31, 1940 begins) is the alternative, and it would put the end one day earlier. The ending is the order's own stated term and the acting instrument is EO 8142 itself. The only operative sentence is the quoted one; the recital states the finding that the public interest requires the exemption and commands nothing else. The recital says the person had already been exempted under EO 7936 of July 30, 1938; those earlier orders predate this one and cannot end it. No later order exempting this person or citing this order is among the held evidence cited here.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Thomas A. Jaggar, Jr., Principal Scientist, National Park Service, Department of the Interior, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year by Executive Order No. 7936 of July 30, 1938, be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby further exempt the said Thomas A. Jaggar, Jr., from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending July 31, 1940.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Clause 1 closes the departments and agencies named in it, and excuses their employees, only for the day or days it names. The clause says the offices "shall be closed all day on" "Monday, July 3, 1939" and that the covered employees "be excused from duty on that day." The exceptions it lists (employees excluded by department heads for special public reasons, or whose absence would be inconsistent with existing law) narrow who is excused but add no further date. The command is limited by its own terms to those dates, so it ended with the last of them, July 3, 1939, recorded inclusive; the wording gives no "until" date, so no exclusive reading arises. The acting instrument is EO 8183 itself, and no later instrument is needed to end it. The command is not an implementation date: the order orders the closing and the excusal for the named day(s).

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order exempts Michael E. Gorman from compulsory retirement for age and fixes its own end in the sentence "hereby exempt the said Michael E. Gorman from compulsory retirement for age for a period of six months ending February 29, 1940". The exemption therefore ran through February 29, 1940, and that date is recorded as the first end, inclusive; the exclusive reading (the exemption ends as February 29, 1940 begins) is the alternative, and it would put the end one day earlier. The ending is the order's own stated term and the acting instrument is EO 8204 itself. The only operative sentence is the quoted one; the recital states the finding that the public interest requires the exemption and commands nothing else. No later order exempting this person or citing this order is among the held evidence cited here.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Michael E. Gorman, Examiner of Indian Inheritance, Office of the Solicitor, Department of the Interior, who, during the month of August, 1939, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of six months:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Michael E. Gorman from compulsory retirement for age for a period of six months ending February 29, 1940.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

July 14, 1939.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order states "is hereby revoked, and such land" returned to the Governor of The Panama Canal, revoking Executive Order No. 2006 of July 30, 1914 (placing land at Darien under the Secretary of the Navy for a naval radio station) and returning the land to the control and jurisdiction of the Governor. The words are in the present tense and state no later effective date, so the revocation and the return of control took effect when the order was made, on September 11, 1939 (the date printed under the signature: "September 11, 1939."). The order was filed on September 12, 1939 and printed in the issue of Wednesday, September 13, 1939 (4 FR 3890); those dates are disclosed as alternative candidates for effectiveness but the order's own text states none. The command is self-executing and was exhausted by performance on issuance, so it is recorded as terminated on that date, with the revoked state of EO 2006 and the return of the land as surviving consequences (see savings). The acting instrument is EO 8250 itself.

EO 8250 (1939-09-11, Franklin D. Roosevelt), "Revocation of Executive Order No. 2006 of July 30, 1914, Placing Certain Land Under the Jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy for Use as a Naval Radio Station" (Canal Zone). Text and identity: the held text is the machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register issue PDF (4 FR 3890, PDF pages 2-2; https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-1939-09-13/pdf/FR-1939-09-13.pdf; PDF sha256 bce26ff5a3f2e529e0eecd6919e8405d44e9ee5e71a0710ad00a8bc42f90abb1), grade original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original true, requires_page_check false; the heading, date and subject match the register row, and the number printed after the signature is OCR-garbled ("[No. 82501" for 8250). I read the whole held text (page images were not inspected). The order has one operative sentence: it revokes EO 2006 and returns the land to the Governor of The Panama Canal. source.quote: Gompers from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1940.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order exempts Samuel J. Gompers from compulsory retirement for age and fixes its own end in the sentence "hereby further exempt the said Samuel J. Gompers from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1940". The exemption therefore ran through September 30, 1940, and that date is recorded as the first end, inclusive; the exclusive reading (the exemption ends as September 30, 1940 begins) is the alternative, and it would put the end one day earlier. The ending is the order's own stated term and the acting instrument is EO 8252 itself. The only operative sentence is the quoted one; the recital states the finding that the public interest requires the exemption and commands nothing else. The recital says the person had already been exempted under EO 7958 of August 19, 1938; those earlier orders predate this one and cannot end it. Later events recorded for this clause: EO 8543 of September 18, 1940 states "I hereby further exempt the said Samuel J. Gompers from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941"; it cites this order by number, grants a further exemption for a later period, and is recorded as a later event; it does not alter the period stated in this order. Its later-events search lists eo 8543 in an "amended by" disposition note; the later order's own text grants a further exemption and leaves this order's stated period unchanged, so the stated date remains the first end under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on "further exempt" orders.

source.quote:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Samuel J. Gompers, Chief Clerk, Department of Labor, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling two years by Executive Orders No. 7958 of August 19, 1938, and No. 8252 of September 14, 1939, be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby further exempt the said Samuel J. Gompers from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

The White House,

September 18, 1940.

that the Foreign Service Regulations of 
the United States be, and they are

lowing as Chapter X  thereof:
CHAPTER X— LEGAL SERVICES
X -l. Duties of officers of the Foreign  
Service in connection with extradition  
proceedings.
(a) Diplomatic representatives.  Dip­
lomatic representatives shall perform 
the following described duties in con­
nection with the extradition from the 
country to which the representative is 
accredited of fugitives from justice in 
the United States:
(1) When so instructed by the De­
partment of State, they shall submit a 
request for the provisional arrest of 
the fugitive either to the foreign office 
or to the competent authority, accord­
ing to local practice.
(2) Upon the receipt of duly authenti­
cated extradition papers from the De­
partment of State, they shall authenti­
cate the certificates of the Department 
of State attached to the papers (unless 
there has been such authentication by 
the diplomatic representative of the re­
quested country at Washington), and 
present the requisition for extradition 
either to the foreign office or to the com­
petent authority of the foreign govern­
ment, according to local practice.
(b) Consular Officers.  In the absence 
of specific instructions from the Depart­
ment of State received either directly or 
through the diplomatic representative, 
consular officers shall not intervene in 
extradition matters. When a consular 
officer is charged with the duty of ap­
plying for extradition, he shall present 
extradition documents to the competent 
authority of the district to which he is 
assigned, and shall act strictly in accord­
ance with instructions from the Depart­
ment of State.

dition papers.  Diplomatic representa­
tives and consular officers of the United

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Clause 1 closes the departments and agencies named in it, and excuses their employees, only for the day or days it names. The clause names two days, "Saturday, December 23, 1939" and "Saturday, December 30,1939" (the second written without a space after the comma in the held text), and excuses the covered employees from duty "on those days." The exceptions it lists narrow who is excused but add no further date. The command is limited by its own terms to those dates, so it ended with the last of them, December 30, 1939, recorded inclusive; the wording gives no "until" date, so no exclusive reading arises. The acting instrument is EO 8291 itself, and no later instrument is needed to end it. The command is not an implementation date: the order orders the closing and the excusal for the named day(s).

research_rationale:
EO 8291 (1939-11-30, Franklin D. Roosevelt), "Excusing Federal Employees From Duty on December 23 and 30, 1939". Text and identity: the held text is the machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register issue PDF (4 FR 4761, PDF pages 1-1; https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-1939-12-05/pdf/FR-1939-12-05.pdf; PDF sha256 88db380459f9b4ebf3d38e9eb67cfccebeda431794e04bdc2facd9920d28735b), grade original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original true, requires_page_check false; its closing line reads "[No. 8291]" and its heading, date and subject match the register row. I read the whole held text (page images were not inspected; the PDF itself is not held in the repository, only its text layer). The order has two numbered clauses: clause 1 (closing of offices and excusal of employees on December 23 and December 30, 1939) and clause 2 (publication in the Federal Register), plus an introductory sentence that commands nothing. Clause 1 expires by its own terms with the last named day, December 30, 1939. Clause 2 was performed by publication in the Federal Register issue of December 5, 1939. The first-end dates are 1939-12-30 and 1939-12-05, so the whole-order end is 1939-12-30. The packet's later-events search (Federal Register disposition notes of 6938 catalog records from 1937 onward, plus operative sentences in 17521 saved order texts) returned no hit for this order, and the held-text number search found no later order citing it. No held source shows an earlier end.

savings_residuals.reason: The order creates no continuing right, status, property or command: its text covers only the closing and excusal on December 23 and 30, 1939 and the publication direction. Any pay or leave consequences of the excused days depend on pay and leave statutes, which the order does not state, and they do not keep the order operative after December 30, 1939.
